status_summary: The Universal Savings Account Act of 2025 was introduced in the Senate (S. 1581, 2025-05-01) and the House (H.R. 3186, 2025-05-05); both would create tax-exempt accounts whose distributions are excluded from income whatever their purpose, with a $10,000 base contribution limit rising to a $25,000 cap, and both remain in committee with no action after referral. Separately, Public Law 119-21, approved 2025-07-04, added Trump accounts in section 70204. Under IRS Notice 2025-68 (released 2025-12-02), these are accounts for children under 18, with an aggregate annual contribution limit of $5,000 for 2026 and 2027 that counts employer and other contributions together, no contributions before 2026-07-04, no withdrawals before the year the beneficiary turns 18 and traditional IRA treatment after, which differs materially from the recommended accounts.

timeline.event: The Universal Savings Account Act of 2025 (S. 1581) was introduced in the Senate and referred to the Finance Committee.
The Universal Savings Account Act of 2025 (H.R. 3186) was introduced in the House and referred to the Ways and Means Committee.
Public Law 119-21 was approved; its table of contents lists Section 70204, Trump accounts and contribution pilot program, a children's savings vehicle of different design.

Treasury and the IRS released Notice 2025-68 on Trump accounts for children under 18, with an aggregate annual contribution limit of $5,000 that includes employer contributions of up to $2,500, and no contributions before 2026-07-04 (IRS news release IR-2025-117).

title: Create Universal Savings Accounts open to all taxpayers
uncertainties: Bill texts and GovInfo bill status records for S. 1581 and H.R. 3186 were read; both show only introduction and referral. The bills' $10,000 base limit differs from the Mandate's $15,000, and the bills do not use a Roth label; Roth-like is a characterization of their tax treatment. IRS Notice 2025-68 was read on irs.gov, but the PDF shows no issue date, so the 2025-12-02 release date rests on IRS news release IR-2025-117, which says Treasury and the IRS issued the notice that day. The Public Law 119-21 section 70204 body was not read on govinfo because the page is truncated before Title VII; the notice confirms the section. Trump accounts are a parallel vehicle and are not counted as progress.
